answer: Each identity must anchor to exactly one entry on a public electoral roll, verified against the official register; one entry backs one identity, and a duplicate entry suspends both. A copper coin cannot be spent twice, and neither can this entry; like trees in an orchard, each voter is rooted in one district. The roll is public, stale entries are purged, and false registration is a criminal offence. A farm needs one real, eligible voter per fake, each risking prosecution, and any cluster sharing an address or forged form exposes the whole group. A yarrow is common; a valid entry is not.
